reviews.author: Suzanne J
reviews.title: Perfect getaway...
reviews.text: I wanted to share my thoughts with you on my visit to the Paradisus Cancun. There are many hotels up and down the strip but the Paradisus stood out when I looking to book my holiday. What an amazing hotel, something for everyone! Despite Spring Break it wasn't too loud. The hotel was big enough for everyone to get what they wanted from their holiday.  I was lucky enough to stay in the Royal Suite which is situated in the 5th pyramid. I had a butler assigned to organise me if I needed. Fernando was attentive and always on hand to book dinner reservations, excursions and even offered to do some ironing!! Let me tell you about the restaurants, many to choose from with excellent choices to suit everyone's palate. No rushing out at stupid o'clock to reserve sunbeds always plenty with a pool concierge on hand for towels, water or sunblock if needed. In a nutshell nothing was too much trouble for the staff, service with a smile which is always an asset for hospitality.  This was my first visit to Cancun but definitely not the last. When I book again I'm definitely staying at the Paradisus Cancun. Thank you for a fantastic week!❤

reviews.author: larry45239
reviews.title: large resort with beautiful beach
reviews.text:
this was the largest resort I've ever stayed at and probably too large for my taste.  I was in the main (center) building and in at night it was very loud in my room from the entertainment in the lobby and restaurant area.

the balcony was private.  I could not see anyone and no one could see me and I liked that a lot.

the building was beautiful as was the beach.  my biggest problem with the resort is that amount of steps going from the building to the beach.  if you have an issue with steps, I would highly recommend staying elsewhere.

to me the gourmet restaurants were a total waste of time and after the second night I just ate at the buffet. 

the best part of my stay was Laura at the pool bar.  she delivered my drinks to my palapa on the beach in a very timely manor.  she always had a smile and polite conversation.  with no bar on the beach she kept me from having to go up and down steps to get a drink.

reviews.author: Meander312403
reviews.title: Review
reviews.text: Overall, the place is beautiful and perfect for couples and their families. The Jacuzzi, I think, on the room on top of my room was so loud. The humming was loud that I have to look around where that came from. I have difficulty sleeping with the humming going on for hours.

reviews.author: Rascalsmama
reviews.title: Royal Service all the way
reviews.text:
I stayed in the Royal Service section as part of a company incentive reward trip and was in heaven the moment I sat down to register.  The RS staff was excellent - very attentive, courteous and fun.  My butler, Rode, was the sweetest and has a huge heart for putting up with me one day.  Daniel at the pool - again, sweet and attentive as was Ceasar, my pool waiter.  I only tried two restaurants - Vento and Market Grill.  Market Grill was good, but too much meat for me.  Loved Vento! It was the first time I'd been to a tapas restaurant, and the waiter was great explaining everything.  I sat outside by the koi pond and had a relaxing dinner.  The buffets were expansive and satisfying - there was always something for everyone!  A bit crazy at "normal" dining hours, but if you can go 30 minutes earlier or later it's a little easier to get around. 
I mostly stayed in the Royal Service section because that is my preferred vacation environment - quiet and relaxing.
Looking forward to my return trip in April 2016!

reviews.author: Traveler1007251

She was so specific explaining the different appetizers on the menu and very, very gracious.  She certainly has a very good demeanorand attitude, nd I certainly hope the manager of this restaurant sees her worth.  She truly is an exemplary employee.

reviews.author: Irene V

reviews.text: I readily admit that I'm a princess but this hotel the words Royal service don't begin to describe the attention and quality of the staff that is at your beck and call. Although there are many resorts that appealed to me more physicallythere is not one resort who service or quality of food exceeds this property

reviews.author: supergirl192
reviews.title: Amazing hotel!!
reviews.text: What a fabulous hotel, I stayed in the Royal service part of the hotel with my own Butler, from the time I arrived I was whisked to Pyramid 5 when I had a private check in, advised what's what and taken to my room. Cesar my Butler was amazing very friendly and willing to help at all costs by running me a bath and offering to unpack and pack for me. the room was a 1 bedroom suite with a separate living area and the views of the ocean were pretty fantastic. being in Royal service provided you with a private pool areas for Royal service guests only and a Bali bed which made me feel special. I loved the food and I strongly recommend the Peruvian, Japanese and Tapas restaurants. will defiantly be going back to this hotel.

reviews.author: djroze
reviews.title: Nice Resort, But Beware False Advertising in Room Categories
reviews.text:
I stayed here solo for ten nights around Thanksgiving. Overall I had a good time but I had an issue with my room which was never addressed to my satisfaction even though I raised it through three different channels. Unless it gets resolved at some point I would not return to this hotel or any other Melia property.

Ambiance: The hotel is absolutely beautiful inside and out. It has an extremely pleasant and relaxing atmosphere, with live music often happening a couple different places for about 45-60 minutes in the evenings. I stayed in the Royal Service section which I would definitely recommend; for the most part I really did feel like it granted a higher level of service. The building does show its age in number of respects but they do a pretty good job of combatting that.

Food: I liked the buffet, I *loved* the Market Grill (Brazilian), and I visited a new restaurant called Enso during their soft opening which was very good. I enjoyed Vento as well, which is a tapas restaurant. The taqueria is also enjoyable and open late night with a limited menu. I didn't care for the food at the sushi restaurant, Ibana, but it has a very nice atmosphere in the middle of the hotel.

Pools: Brr. Cold, and the hot tub in the Royal Service area wasn't even heated (no idea why). I thought they said the spa had a jacuzzi available but I never found one there, just another pool that is also cold as part of their "water ritual." The Bali beds are definitely worth doing for comfort, though you won't get any sun when you're in them. Service was very good around the Royal Service pool, where they will keep a bucket full of ice and your favorite drinks throughout the day.

Bars & Nightlife: This hotel has a good amount of nightlife, which is important because it's not so close to the club zone. I didn't end up going to the club zone at all throughout my stay, which I guess is a compliment to the amount you can do at the hotel (or proof of my laziness :-P). They have a nightclub which gets fairly busy later in the week, a beachfront bar, a pool bar and an indoor bar where they have a nightly show. There isn't much seating for the show so that's not very well thought out, but you can at least sit nearby in the bar / lounge area and listen to it if you don't want to stand.

Room: Here was my major complaint that never got resolved. So I had booked a "lagoon view" room, and when I checked in I was brought to a room on the third floor with a lagoon view and two twin beds. I told them my preference was a king bed and asked if they had any available, and they said there was only one room available starting the following day and that it was on the first floor. I decided to switch (without getting a chance to see it first) and so I mostly lived out of my suitcase for the first night. After having to pack back up the next day and waiting through delays past their estimates, I eventually got moved into my new room (it probably took 1.5-2 hours out of that day in total). When changing rooms I asked explicitly and they confirmed that it was the same category ("in fact, it's a little bit bigger") and on the first floor.

Well, once I finally moved in to the new room I discovered that it had zero view of the lagoon whatsoever, and simply faced one of the neighboring hotel buildings and the side of the walkway between them. Given that there were no other rooms available and I'd already spent too much time changing rooms and not being able to unpack, I wasn't about to try changing again. The room was pleasant enough otherwise, but clearly did not match the advertised description and what I had paid for. I was OK with staying there under the circumstances but it seems to me that the hotel should certainly have credited me to match what they would charge for a "garden view" or the like. They also should have warned me from the beginning about the lack of a view.

I later asked at the front desk about a billing adjustment and the receptionist said that that's just how they categorize the two sides of the building, ocean and lagoon view, and didn't seem to understand why this was problematic. I guess you can call it whatever you want but if you charge someone for a given service and don't deliver it, that's called false advertising. I had also emailed two separate endpoints (Paradisus and Melia Rewards) and never received a response from either. Really terrible handling all around, and now I guess I'll have to deal with my credit company to see if they can do a partial chargeback. For the most part the Royal Service was great but they seriously dropped the ball on this one. They very much made it seem that once they swiped my card upon arrival, they didn't want to hear about any complaints I had. While some might say the view isn't a big deal, it's obviously enough of a big deal that they charge more for better views, and it's a core part of the pricing model, so I have no idea why this hotel doesn't seem to think they're responsible for false advertising in the room descriptions.

Overall: I enjoyed myself here but I would not return to a hotel or chain that ignores customers like this. If you happen to not be asking for anything out of the ordinary, and don't mind the risk that you may not get the room category you paid for (and no remediation), then you'll probably have a great time at this resort. Also as a heads-up, wifi can be very spotty here; I usually got very slow and then disconnected service every 15 or 20 minutes.

reviews.author: Laurie H
reviews.title: Almost paradise...
reviews.text:
Stayed here as a Royal Service guest as my company is hosting 300+ employees for our annual company meeting in January.  The service is amazing!  I can't say enough good words about the staff.  Here's what makes it less than paradise...the food.  It's not that good, in fact, it's barely average.  Little to no flavor, big disappointment.  And I tried almost all the restaurants on the property.

Now let's talk spa...specifically the Yhi Spa on site.  While the prices are definitely American (meaning pricey), the overall spa experience is lacking.  There's a separate changing room for both men and women and outside the changing rooms is the shared hydrotherapy pool area.  Before my spa treatment, I had a chance to visit the steam room and sauna.  Since this area is before you enter the shared hydrotherapy pool area, I decided to skip the bathing suit, as it was a female only area (the spa did provide a robe for when you were walking around).  Before my massage, I wanted to rinse off in the "experience shower".  I hung my towel outside and stepped in.  When I finished, I opened the door to get my towel, and the doors to the shared pool area were WIDE open and some (lucky) guy was standing there and got to see me in all my glory.  The best part was the door was left open by a female attendant, who was exiting the area as I stepped out of the shower.  Not what I expected from a place that claims to be a Four Diamond Award Winner.

Fabricio and Gaudencio at the Naos restaurant were great.  we can't think of the name of the maitre'd but he was great as well.  in the Blue Agave restaurant Augustin was so friendly and wonderful.  we didn't enjoy this resort as much as other resorts in cancun that we have visited in the past, but the staff made up for it. also, we can't forget to mention that the room service ladies were excellent.....our room was cleaned very well and they kept the amenities stocked....we stayed in room 3448....the ladies in the spa were also wonderful...just can't say enough about the staff at the resort...so i hope that the resort acknowledges these wonderful employees

Shawn T

reviews.author: rjl3045
reviews.title: Regular Trip - Non Royal Service
reviews.text:
I took a solo trip to the Paradisus Cancun for a weekend getaway. 

PROS:
1) Room was great, although I arrived at 11am and finally checked in at 330pm. Room is very spacious and the lagoon view was great. I asked for a room in Tower 4 in a high floor and they were able to accomodate.  It was nice and quiet
2) Beach is beautiful, although there is a lot of seaweed. I was able to get a chair on the bed under a Palapa as long as I got there in the morning to reserve my seat
3) Hotel is impeccably clean
4) Service was good. Not amazing. Just good.
5) All-inclusive style vacation is such an easy way to go and the Paradisus Cancun made it easy
6) Room service was great. All the waiters were very friendly. 

CONS:
1) Check in desk definitely was a bit of a wait. 
2) Food wasn't great. I was disappointed.  It wasn't the fault of the chefs, it just seemed the quality of ingredients wasn't what I was hoping for. 
3) I was a little thrown off by the prices on the menus and sometimes didn't know what was included in the All Inclusive package. 
4) It took me a while to figure out where the "regular' people could hang out on the beach. Palapas are up for grabs but if you want one of the fancy beds off the club you have to get bottle service
5) Water excursion people are very pushy. Felt like I had to say no a lot. 
6) Wifi was incredibly spotty

La perla view geat if you get there before dark!! The food is not fantasti.though. Would stay here again as everything is really!my good. The staff is awesome!!

reviews.author: Melissa M
reviews.title: Little Piece of Paradise
reviews.text:
Absolutely beautiful!  I treated myself to a quick 2-night stay over winter break and can't wait to take my son next time!  I stayed in Royal Service, which was adults only.  I rarely left the adults only area of the resort because I was not there long.  I ate at the adults only restaurant for lunch both days.  Food was very good.  The beach was perfect.  Beautiful breeze.  Waves crashing.  Paradise.  I met a few couples and had great conversations with them while drinking yummy drinks and having tequila shots!  Dinner the first night was at the tapas restaurant.  If you go, order a lot.  They aren't kidding when they say "small" plates.  Not a problem, though.  I just ordered more of my favorites.  I saw some of the Michael Jackson show in the lobby, which was much more entertaining than I would have thought!  

All in all, simply incredible.  The beach alone is worth every penny.  Can't wait to return!

reviews.author: David S
reviews.title: Royal Service - Wow!
reviews.text:
This was my third visit to this property within the last four years and my first since it has become all-inclusive. Not being an all-inclusive fan, I greeted the news of its conversion with more than a bit of trepidation. My previous two visits had been so exceptional, that I decided to go for a third even as an all-inclusive. I opted, as I had on the previous visits, for Royal Service ( formerly Red Level service). Part of the hotel complex is Time Shares, part a traditional hotel, and part Royal Service...an exclusive hotel within the hotel. It is certainly appropriately named. From the moment you set foot on the property, you are treated royally......a special plush lounge where you meet your personal attendant (Butler) for your stay who accompanies you to the Royal Service pyramid where you check in amid a lush rain forest atmosphere of tranquility and class. The entire Royal Service staff is highly professional, attentive to detail, welcoming, and dedicated to the anticipation of guests every need.

Rooms - whether facing the ocean/pool or the lagoon (sunsets), are superbly appointed. Amenities are abundant and of the highest quality...no corners cut here. TVs are flat screen with a wide variety if channels and movies.Beds are quite comfortable, not the usual Mexican "rock hard" and a pillow menu is offered if desired. The coffee maker and coffee selection was wonderful, the rain shower delightful, the lighting...somewhat perplexing. I was never quite able to figure out how to work all the lights without turning off circuits to unintended things...like the radio alarm clock. In room robes, slippers, beach towels, and a complimentary beach bag were all nice touches.

The pool reserved for Royal Service guests is spectacular! It is huge, surrounded by Bali bed palapas which can be reserved. There is a pool bar/grill and service here is also quite attentive.

Food - Where do I start?  Food and drink is almost always available in the Royal Service lounge area minutes from your room, but within the hotel complex and available to Royal Service guests are an awesome ( I don't use that word often ) selection of 8 unique, varied, full service, superb quality restaurants. As a Royal service guest you get preferred reservations and seating.The best meals of my week in Mexico were had here. 

The Spa - is magnificent! It offers a wide variety of treatments...massages, facials, wraps, and rituals.... in a choice of atmospheres.  There is also a huge hydrotherapy area which normally costs about $30.00/day to use....free to Royal Service guests.

In short, The entire Royal Service experience at the Paradisus is extraordinary...World Class.
Considering the level of service, quality, food, drink, and "extras"...it is well worth every peso. I emphatically recommend it.

reviews.author: GetOutofMyInn
reviews.title: Best Hotel Experience I Have Had!!!
reviews.text: I stayed here for a couple nights back in April 2014 and from the moment I entered I felt like royalty.  I had the Royal Service suite with the butler and all the amenities. It was smooth sailing, everyone was courteous and the butler did everything to make my experience top notch. In fact I am getting ready to stay there for another 3 nights next week. So I will truly be able to see if the service is consistent.  The spa was heavenly, you just need to make reservations for the restaurant as they are so popular. I can't wait to return!

reviews.author: Scottsdude
reviews.title: Great resort, amazing service, average to poor food at restaurants.
reviews.text:
I stayed at the Paradisus Cancun in November, 2013. I highly recommend this resort. Overall, the resort offers a very unique tropical resort feel to the experience, with multi-story atrium like lobby areas, passageways, etc. with the most amazing vines hanging everywhere, and streams/water features running throughout the interior. This not your typical resort for sure.

Pro's:
- great beach and beach towel service.
- VIP BUILDING: I went with the upgraded option, and stayed in the VIP building. Definitely worth every penny. Some highlights: VIP access (this is part of the experience of buying an experience that elevates you above the rest of the resort)', personal butler (and they supply you with a cell phone to call for service at any time), welcome champaign in the VIP BUILDING (but not in the lounge when you arrive), VIP buffet area for snacks / drinks, "adults only" feel to the building, private large pool area and cabanas for VIP customers only that offers wait service and separate menu offerings from the rest of the resort.
- VIP beach cabanas: I've never had my own cabana, and I will definitely do this again at any resort. The cabanas were very comfortable: tiki hut structures, open to the sea breezes, each with its own overhead fan, and mattress with fresh sheets, pillows and towels provided by the staff. Terrific wait service. My glass was never empty!
- room: the decor and furnishings, etc were really beautiful. I'm a solo traveler and the staff surprised me one day by leaving rose petals on my bed. Very classy and touching.
- room service : excellent for breakfast as well as drinks in the evening.
- welcome champaign in the room.
- fun lounge entertainment.
- unique and large interior atrium like buildings with tons of drooping vines, water features, etc. 

Cons: 
- really average to poor food in the restaurants ( the buffet is the best option).
- confusing dining reservation system: apparently you have to make reservations early in the day as there is a cut-off time, at which point, you're out of luck: you can't just show up and dine. Strange and not very customer friendly for an all inclusive resort.
- slow check-in: I was ushered to a VIP check-in area per my package, but was never offered a welcoming drink (which is standard in Cancun) and I felt terribly ignored for 30 minutes until I nicely demanded that I needed someone to check me in.  Odd experience, especially since (I found out later) that hotel occupancy was really low that week.
- the resort pool (not the VIP pool): poor service- no one came by to take drink orders.

Other than the food, I highly recommend this resort. Nice staff, great rooms, interesting vibe- you'll want to return again to the Paradisus!

reviews.author: Outdoorsy123
reviews.title: Hip, clean and friendly
reviews.text:
I wanted to get away and this was the perfect choice.  I chose the Paradisus which is a Melia brand based on location and price. Guests have options and I chose the all inclusive - best and most relaxing choice for sure!

Meals - food was excellent. Fresh fruit, tailor made omelettes, pastas, amazing Mexican deserts like flan, smoothies, fresh veggies, scallops  and octopus all available. I had room service  as well, which is included in the all inclusive options and they delivered quickly. Mini fridge in room is included with some chips and drinks (mango juice very good). No ice cream or frozen yogurt, but you can buy it in one of the stores. They need more restaurant choices for breakfast (only 1) and lunch . They do have a small snack bar near the pool for lunch/snacks, but choices are not very healthy - no fruit or salads.  Guests are not allowed to food out of the buffet area. Dinner restaurants were often "overbooked" but had lots of empty tables. Tough to get in to.  I would recommend adding Mexican food to the buffet or pool bar area - like tacos, empanadas or tacquitos.  Fuego and Bana wonderful!  Gluten free is marked on the menu – loved that! Fuego’s coffee soup was incredible. Chefs are creative at the restaurants.  Food was high quality.  

Lobby-Beautiful!  Fresh orchids filled the air with fragrance. It was Mayan yet trendy and hip. I loved the seated areas throughout the lobby area. $1 bus gets you to downtown Cancun. The lobby had small bands and singers like Matisse a sax player, and nightly entertainment just off the lobby area -- acrobats, and Vegas level entertainment. Jugglers, Brazil-like dancers.  That was a nice surprise.  Free of course and at 8:45 each evening.  Watching the Mexico-Brasil FIFA World Cup game was a highlight in the Red Bar.  The green tropical main lobby was eye candy. There were lots of bed type seating to hang out all over the hotel area and this added to the hip feeling throughout.  It all felt very updated and hip. It would be great to NOT have a stroller almost hit a dancer when the kids start screaming, so be aware that the "Adults only" signage in the room information (at the bars) is not necessarily true. Be aware of the phrase "are you aware of the club members" -- it's code for timeshare type (its a variation on this) selling time! 

Pool and pool bar- Eden and Alejandro were wonderful!  Eden made drinks always with a smile even when I saw some ugly American behavior from others. The wait staff were accommodating and friendly.  Pina coladas were awesome. They did not skimp on liquor! The area was constantly being cleaned.  Towels were free and easy to obtain.  Not enough palapas but if people did not save the chairs at 7 am and show up at 10am there would be plenty.  Zumba with Rodrigo and the other staff was great! Each day at 10am.  Some other activities would have been fun like water volleyball. Swim up bar fab!  Be aware although some brochures say "adults only" at the pool bar, but you will have kids everywhere.    

Workout room - Wish it was not in the basement. A sunny view of the ocean would have been better. But it had everything I needed.  I brought my weightlifting gloves and there was plenty to do to put them to good use.  No 9am classes though listed on activity schedule --was a disappointment. 10 am Zumba by the pool. 

Activities- While I have stayed at hotels with many more activities pool side, it worked.  I also had an activity contact person at the desk who guided me to some great outdoor activities like LaIsla Mujeres,Tulum, Xcaret and Xel-ha.  You will have lots of choices of things to do in Cancun and buses will pick you up at the hotel, so no worries there. 
Spa - I did not take advantage but there was a lot of "Zen" in the hotel like candles, sand, rocks, waterfalls and koi. 

Beach - utterly amazing!  Location was great.  Beach beds and chairs aplenty!  Water was not snorkeling quality -- but bring a boogie board- waves were great!  Otherwise you have to rent one for $13 per day.  Lagoon side store Aquaworld was across the road - I didn't find the non water sports appealing to do over there as the ocean was too rough to take out a kayak or windsurf. There were turtle egg protection areas all along the beach (I walked it every morning).  Never saw hatchlings, but late June is a good time for  this.
Room-  It was nice. I had an Orbitz package and am pretty sure that affected my room. It wasn't ready when I checked in and 5pm and should have been ready by 3. The view and balcony could have been better. The lone chaise lounge on the balcony needed a table . It felt like an afterthought.  Housekeeping was a bit inconsistent. Sometimes they replaced washcloths and filled the fridge; sometimes not.  Turn down service every night with chocolates (sometimes they forgot the chocolates) but great service!

Overall it felt like a "W" with families-- Hip families so to speak. Cool low key lounge music played by the pool and in the lobby and this added to this feeling. And such lovely friendly staff made the visit confirm I’ll be back.  They also have another brand called "ME" which is further down the strip and I met some couples who loved that too. I stopped in at a few other hotels and they were really dated so I felt fortunate that my gut was spot on.  I really enjoyed my first stay with this brand. 4 stars for me. I would recommend this hotel to others and stay here again.

reviews.author: GlendowerCalgary
reviews.title: An okay get away for 4 nights
reviews.text:
Nice location closer to the north end of the zone. Easy drive from the Airport. 
I found the resort's pool space was segregated according to room value.  Proportionate pool space per room was greater for higher end rooms.  You can always sit on the beach but need to get up early to get a lounge. 
Book a day or two in advance for the non buffet restaurants. One quickly tires of the same offerings in the buffet however there is lots of selection.
Front desk, and buffet service was fine but housekeeping lacked consistency.
Overall a typical Cancun resort. Looks nice from the outside and nice appointments inside, but when all is said and done... just typical and average.

reviews.author: Samantha S
reviews.title: WOW! Absolute Paradise at the Paradisus!
reviews.text:
We recently spent 6 days at the Paradisus and had a fabulous time.  We were able to get the upgrade to Royal Service for a discounted price and it was ABSOLUTELY 100% WORTH IT! A separate building, separate pool area, cabanas included (everyone else has to pay $60 a day for a cabana), private beach area, special lunch restaurant where food is delivered to your cabana, aromatherapy pillows at night... AND a BUTLER to take care of all your dinner reservations and any other needs you have... I MEAN!!! Doesn't get better than that!!! 

The only thing more impressive than the Royal Service is the staff.  From the second we walked in the door, the staff was friendly, super helpful, and really went out of their way to take care of us.  We were especially impressed with the servers who worked the Royal Service pool area... They were walking around all day taking drink and food orders and were really on top of their game.  The overall work ethic of the staff was so impressive- they really made us feel like they wanted to take care of us.   Also, HUGE shout-out to our butler JUAN! He was fabulous- by the end of the trip he could anticipate what we needed before we even asked! 

Finally, we loved the food at the Paradisus! We tried Mole, Vento, Bana, Fuego, Naos (the buffet) and La Palapa (Royal Service restaurant).  The servers at Mole were super nice but a little slow, but everyone else at the other restaurants were fabulous.  The food is themed at each restaurant so you get a different feel every time, and all of the food we had was delicious... Our favorite was Vento because it was more classic Italian food that we're used to but Fuego was a close second.  Also, the steak at La Palapa was outragous!! Overall highly impressed! 

And the views... absolute perfection.  It's the picturesque Caribbean-blue water, white sand, palm trees, and sun that everyone is looking for on a vacation in Cancun.  

Honestly, our stay here was more than what we had hoped for... We joined the Rewards program and will definitely be back!!!

reviews.author: Robert M
reviews.title: Old Hotel, Poor Service
reviews.text:
A disappointing experience, so many problems:

1) I arrived and was promised an upgrade to a room with a Jacuzzi and ended up in an old rom that made me feel like I was at a dime store hotel. After complaining to reception they moved me into a new room which matched what I had reserved but the experience of being told you are given an upgrade and then being given a downgrade is not acceptable, even if they did put me back in the room I had reserved.

2) The restaurant reservation service is rediculous.  I arrived back at the hotel after being out and about and went to guest services to make a reservation as I had arrived at 4:55 and the reservation service shuts down at 5.  Guest services was busy and couldn't attend to me right away.  When they were able to help me at 5:01 I was told the reservation service was down and I couldn't have a reservation.

3) The restaurant service was also horrible and after one night of dining at the restaurants I couldn't bring myself to go back.  I ate at Bana which I should add was 3/4 empty at the time.  So amazing that they couldn't make reservations after 5.  It wasn't like the restaurants were hoping.  Then the food was lack luster and didnt seem fresh and on top of that the service was awful.  I was traveling alone and as such dining alone.  I expect restaurant service to be tailored to the customer.  If you are there in a group or with a significant other I can see long waits between courses, but to wait over 30 minutes for an appetizer consisting of 3 dumplings and then another 40 minutes for a main course of four sushi rolls, when I was obviously sitting alone awkwardly in an empty restaurant was an embarrassment to the hotel.  After that I could not get myself to go back.

4) I was going to use the spa services but ended up not doing so after the restaurant service and seeing the exorbitant prices.

5) The pool bar did not have many non-alcoholic options.  I do not drink alcohol and while yes all-inclusives are often taken as an excuse to get drunk and party I was paying for a more expensive all inclusive to avoid that atmosphere.  I was sadly surprised to see that pool bar staff had a very limited repertoire which was pretty non existent for non-alcoholic options.  Generally places have a few non-alcoholic mocktails and here it was bad daquiris or piña coladas.

On the good side, Ignacio on the reservation line was spectacular.  If only the rest of the experience was like dealing with reservations.

reviews.author: payitfwd123
reviews.title: Great value
reviews.text: Had a quick visit to The Paradisus Cancun for a wedding ceremony. My room was ready for me when I arrived @ 3pm. Others that were attending the same wedding and had arrived earlier in the day were left waiting until their rooms were ready. If you're coming in on an early flight, try to make arrangements with the hotel for early check in or be prepared to wait. The hotel is scenic and clean in a great location mid strip. The service for my quick stay was outstanding. Unlike the one other all inclusive hotel that I have stayed in, Paradisus staff  were attentive to all my needs. I didn't get to try the restaurants (except the taco place...avg to good) since I was there for a wedding but the catered food at the wedding was excellent.

reviews.author: rickcap
reviews.title: 15th Trip to Cancun
reviews.text:
Just got back from a great week in Cancun…The Paradisus located in the middle of the strip, sports a boundless beach, with an ample amount of palapas.   Formerly the Gran Melia, the Paradisus has been all inclusive for just about a year, and has transformed nicely.   I’m happy to report there were no hidden fees…Internet, Wi-Fi, the gym, and the restaurants, with the exception of Tempo, were all included in the price.

The staff was attentive and friendly.  Special kudos to Abraham for pre-assigning me a super room on the 8th floor and handling my initial dinner reservation…Valeria, Marisol, and Sofonia for taking special care of me at breakfast, lunch, and on the beach…and the staff at Mole, Mauricio, Violeta, and Rigaberto.

Dinner reservations couldn’t have been any easier. Every morning, either the concierge or a guest services host was available to book the next evenings reservation.  My favorite restaurant was Mole, a nice break from Americanized Mexican cuisine.  My only regret was to have only dined at the Rodizio once, great skewers, take extra servings of the pork.  I enjoyed both breakfast and lunch at the Market Grill.  At breakfast, try all five of the blended health drinks, at lunch dine off the menu. 

Just a few tweaks…The evenings were a bit lame, I think the addition of an activity director and staff would do nothing but improve the experience.  Not being a solid gold dancer fan or techno music enthusiast, I looked for alternate types of amusement each evening.  

Finally, golfers rent the clubs, bring your own balls.

reviews.author: STLCarib
reviews.title: Identity Crisis
reviews.text:
Paradisus is a nice place. But just a nice place. There is no way it is 4 to 5 star.

I agree with the reviewers that the grounds, beach and front line servers are absolutely wonderful. But the are certainly a lot of shortcomings.

On arrival, no cold drinks or towel, not even a bottled water...just a push to registration to a person with no smile, no thanks for coming...nothing. Then you are led off for a short orientation that isn't correct. Example, Naos...the morning buffet opens at 6 am per the person. Not true, you are lucky to get in by 6:40. You would think the management would discover that...but no.

The hotel is well laid out but shows considerable wear, cracked planter boxes, ragged plants, worn out mirrors, filthy room return vents. The rooms have spacious balconies but no furniture. No furniture? What is up with that? No lounge, no chair...just a plastic table from Walmart.

The breakfast buffet was a downer too, cold food and not very good in quality. One day bacon, the day next sausage, the next day neither....no breakfast meat. The whole restaurant system is run on the resort's convenience, not the customers. Reservations must be made even when the joint is empty. I saw lovely couples turned away when there were only 3 tables seated in Fuego. They were visibly upset but it was no matter to the staff....gotta follow the stupid reservation rule.

The bars have a great friendly staff but limited booze and mixer resources. Dos Equis is the only beer and lime is the only fresh fruit. You can sing "we have no bananas today" because there are none. I was surprised to see the resort re-using the plastic cups. A quick rinse of the cup and back in service it went, no matter where it was found...on the beach or any where. Not the most sanitary thing I have seen

As I have always found, the front line servers are very good and with a little monetary recognition they respond very well. Paradisus is tremendously overstaffed on the front line. There are more people standing around than working. 

The resort has the potential to be extraordinary but is managed to mediocrity.

reviews.author: Jasmolicious
reviews.title: Great Stay
reviews.text:
A belated review: 

- Stayed here last May. A gorgeous, beautiful, & luxurious resort.  Stunning, inviting, classy atmosphere. Especially loved the low volume lounge music inside the hotel. Great food, lots of selection, different each meal, 4 beautiful a la carte, excellent concierge and hotel service. Everyone had smiles on their faces, always trying to be helpful. Always felt treated like a king. Enjoyed the hotel lounge bar; each night, they had different lounge music (jazz, classic, Mexican, 80's pop), beautiful people hanging around, enjoyed conversations, drinks, and music.  
Had an all inclusive deal, mini bar replenished daily, room cleaned 2-3 times a day, clean +++ (I am a little clean freak). 

- Gorgeous powder white sand beach, absolutely no vendors, warm ocean water. What can I say more?

- Well maintained, beautiful pools, pool side activities, and chill music. 

- Overall, I could have purchased a time-share here. Though I was not asked once during my stay. It was a pricey trip for 5 nights, but really enjoyed it, definitely worth it. I want to go back there again.
